section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
The second day of Rosh HaShanah,
the year 5728.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse and the Alter Rebbe's and Mitteler Rebbe's precise analyses of the phrase "great shofar" and the anonymous blower.
section.t: "And it shall be on that day, a great shofar will be blown, and those lost in the land of Ashur and those cast away in the land of Mitzrayim will come and bow down to Hashem on the holy mountain in Yerushalayim."
And the Alter Rebbe precisely analyzes
(in the maamar beginning with this phrase in Likkutei Torah)
what is said: "with a great shofar,"
[asking] what is the quality of a great shofar.
Also, one must understand
(as he precisely analyzes later in the maamar)
what is said: "will blow" [yitka] without specifying who is the blower.
And the Mitteler Rebbe
adds another precise point in this: that it says "yitka,"
for the term "yitka"
(with a kamatz under the tav)
indicates that it will blow of itself.
And the point of the explanation
(in the discourses)
is,
that the arousal through a plain shofar is only for those who are somewhat close,
and in order to arouse those lost in the land of Ashur and those cast away in the land of Mitzrayim, that they too will be aroused to come to Yerushalayim and bow down to Hashem,
it is through a great shofar.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the superiority of the great shofar over the plain shofar, relating to the revelation of the innermost aspect of Divinity beyond all connection to worlds.
section.t: And in order to explain the superiority of the great shofar that will be in the future,
the maamar prefaces
an explanation of the concept of the shofar of Rosh HaShanah
(now),
that through Israel blowing the shofar,
which is the cry of the innermost heart beyond intellect,
through this is drawn down the innermost heart above, so to speak,
the supernal will that is above wisdom.
And about this it is said,
"And my Lord Hashem will blow the shofar,"
for just as the blowing of the shofar by a person is the cry of the innermost heart,
so too is it above,
for the concept of blowing the shofar is the drawing down and revelation of the innermost aspect.
And the difference between a plain shofar and a great shofar is,
that a plain shofar is the drawing down and revelation of the innermost aspect of Elokus that is above worlds but is related to worlds,
Sovev Kol Almin,
and a great shofar is the drawing down and revelation of the innermost aspect of Elokus that is above any relation to worlds,
above even Sovev.
And this is that regarding a plain shofar it is written "And my Lord Hashem will blow the shofar,"
for "my Lord Hashem" are Names,
except that these Names
("my Lord Hashem" vocalized with the vowels of Elokim)
are most sublime,
and regarding the great shofar it is written "will blow" [yitka] without specifying who is the blower,
for this blowing is a drawing down and revelation from the aspect of the Hidden of All Hidden,
which is above Names.
